title: Hosted API — Unit Econ Sensitivity & Batch Opportunities (draft)
summary: Working sensitivity model and actionable recommendations to reduce Hosted API marginal COGS and improve gross margin across models and regions. Focus areas: batching, cache utilization, quantization tradeoffs, regional capacity pricing, and pricing tiers for high-volume customers.
body:
Purpose:
- Build a compact, defensible sensitivity spreadsheet for Hosted API unit economics (per-token COGS, margin by model and region) that product and finance can iterate on.
- Identify high-impact operational levers (batching, prefix caching, quantization) and prioritize experiments to capture at least 12–18% unit-cost reduction on long-tail workloads.

Key assumptions (base case):
- Example models: rw-13b, rw-33b, rw-70b-qat (8-bit), community-7b.
- GPU hourly blended COGS by region: us-west (p100-style): $1.60/hr, us-east: $1.75/hr, eu-west: $1.90/hr, ap-sg: $2.40/hr (includes infra + amortized infra costs).
- Average effective tokens per request (hosted mix): 120 tokens (prompt + gen).
- KV cache hit-rate baseline: 18% (warm prefixes).
- Average batch size baseline: 1.6 requests/batch (observed low due to low-latency SLOs and single-request traffic).
- Pricing input (list price per 1k tokens): varies by model (we map to plan tiers elsewhere).

Per-token COGS snapshot (base case, simplified):
- rw-13b: 0.00095 USD/token (GPU amortized + infra + network)
- rw-33b: 0.00145 USD/token
- rw-70b-qat: 0.00190 USD/token
- community-7b: 0.00040 USD/token

Primary drivers and sensitivity notes:
1) Batch size moves (most impact for throughput-oriented customers):
   - Increasing average batch size to 4.0 reduces per-token cost by ~26–32% for rw-13b and rw-33b depending on sequence length distribution.
   - Opportunity: server-side batching + client SDK guidance could target 2.5x current batching within 90 days for batchable workloads (embeddings/large-batch generation).

2) KV/prefix caching:
   - Moving KV hit-rate from 18% -> 45% yields ~9–12% COGS improvement for chat workloads where prefixes are repeated.
   - Action: provide per-route cache hints and a small dedicated cache tier for enterprise customers (configurable TTLs).

3) Quantization and model variants:
   - 8-bit quantized rw-70b (qat) shows 18–22% cost improvement vs fp16 for long contexts at similar quality on our evals.
   - Tradeoff: edge cases in safety/quality need guardrails. Recommend A/B production test on <10% of traffic before wide rollout.

4) Region-aware capacity pricing:
   - Ap-sg region COGS currently ~+34% vs us-west due to spot availability and egress premiums.
   - Price anchoring: introduce region-specific surcharge and/or cross-region routing controls for latency-sensitive customers.

Sensitivity scenario table (representative, not exhaustive):
- Scenario A (base): batch 1.6, cache 18% -> rw-13b cost 0.00095 USD/token
- Scenario B (batch 3.0): batch 3.0, cache 18% -> rw-13b cost ~0.00070 USD/token (-26%)
- Scenario C (batch 3.0 + cache 45%): rw-13b cost ~0.00062 USD/token (-35%)
- Scenario D (quantized models adopted broadly): rw-70b-qat cost -20% vs base rw-70b

Practical experiments to run (90-day horizon):
- Experiment 1: "Batching opt-in" beta. Provide SDK flag to enable client-side request aggregation for batched generation and embeddings. Metric: avg batch size, token/sec, 95th latency, per-token COGS. Target: avg batch size >=2.5 on beta customers. (Owner: SDK + Hosting)
- Experiment 2: "Route-level KV caching". Expose cache hinting headers and measure hit-rate lift. Target: increase global hit-rate to 30% for routes that are amenable. (Owner: Serving-runtime)
- Experiment 3: "Quantized model rollout". Canary 8-bit variants for 70b class with quality checks (eval suite). Monitor hallucinations/regressions and cost. (Owner: Applied-ML + Serving)
- Experiment 4: "Region routing policy". Pilot dynamic routing to lower-cost region with optional latency tradeoff for selected customers. (Owner: Platform)

Pricing / margin implications:
- With combined batching (3x) + caching (40% hit-rate) + 8-bit adoption where applicable, estimated blended COGS reduction: 28–36% across hosted API traffic mix.
- For 2026 ARR planning exercise: apply scenario uplift to current revenue buckets to show margin expansion potential and required engineering investment (FTE + infra).

Operational blockers & open questions:
- SLO implications: server-side batching can increase P95 latency for interactive requests. Need to define classes of traffic that are batchable vs interactive and enforce policy.
- Billing granularity: current billing per-token vs per-request metering changes required to capture batching discounts for customers. Finance alignment needed.
- Observability gaps: token-level cost attribution by route/model currently has 10–15% noise. Invest in tracing/label fidelity.

Recommended next steps (priority ordered):
1) Ship SDK aggregation flag + run small beta (30 days to deliver minimal SDK + server toggle).
2) Implement and instrument route-level KV caching and expose a dashboard for hit-rate per route.
3) Start quantized canary on low-risk routes; hold for quality gate.
4) Finance + Product: draft pricing annex for region surcharges and bundle discounts for reserved capacity customers.

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- SDK aggregation flag: Jordan Reyes (30d)
- Route cache headers + dashboard: Lina Markovic (45d)
- Quantized model canary & eval suite: Ethan Goldberg + Applied-ML (60d)
- Pricing annex draft: Aisha Patel + Finance (14d)

Notes-to-self / discussion points for next review:
- Need to map real customer request distributions into the sensitivity model (more long-tail analysis).
- Consider introducing a small per-request base charge for interactive single-token calls to reduce price sensitivity and encourage batching.
- Validate GPU price assumptions with Infra procurement (longer-term reserved pricing may shift COGS materially).

Appendix: quick reference numbers (for spreadsheet inputs)
- Blended infra hourly cost estimates by model-size (per concurrency bucket) — see tab "Per-token-COGS-by-model"
- Latency impact model: P50 vs P95 delta as batch size increases — see tab "Batching-scenarios"
- Customer segmentation for experiments: 1) interactive (chat widgets), 2) high-throughput (embeddings), 3) scheduled/reporting (batch jobs)

Footer: This is a living draft intended to feed Optimize roadmap and next quarterly planning. Please add comments inline in Confluence page linked above or open OPT tickets for follow-ups.
